text.p: - Slovenian, Italian and Hungarian foreign secretaries, who met in Maribor in Slovenia on Wednesday, paved the way for a tighter cooperation between the three countries in defence, transport, economy and culture.
- Campaigning for parliamentary elections starts officially on Thursday, one month ahead of the November 10 vote.

- The parliament on Thursday decided the government has to determine additional companies that will join in the voucher privatisation process by January 1997, as the amount of vouchers significantly exceeds the amount of capital available.
- Debt-ridden shoe factory Peko resumed production on Wednesday after a one-day break, reaching a debt rescheduling agreement with its main creditor bank Gorenjska banka.
- Czech holding ICEC said it would start paper production in Videm Krsko within two weeks. ICEC bought Videm at an auction in March.
- Experts from NATO and Partnership for Peace countries will start a two-day meeting in Ljubljana on Thursday in order to discuss the need for democratic control over army forces.
- Only 18 percent of Slovenians say they are better off than five years ago, while 49 percent believe they are worse off, an opinion poll showed.
- One out of three Slovenians has been involved in a court case at a regular or a minor offences court, the Supreme Court said.
- A prosecutor has indicted textile producer Tkanina because of allegeded irregularities in its 1991 privatisation.
- Sources in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia claim the government is considering normalising its relations with Slovenia.
